answer.reason: Gibeah of Benjamin is the setting of two defining events: the outrage against the Levite's concubine that led to war, and its destruction by Israel; it was also Saul's home.

clauses.english: was where the men of the city abused the Levite's concubine, and she died
clauses.quote: the men of Gibeah rose against me, and beset the house round about upon me by night

clauses.english: was attacked by Israel after Benjamin refused to give up its wicked men, and was smitten with the sword
clauses.quote: smote all the city with the edge of the sword

clauses.english: was the home of King Saul, to which he went after being chosen king
clauses.quote: Saul also went home to Gibeah

doubts: Some verses naming Gibeah in Judges 19-20, 1 Samuel and Hosea may concern a different Gibeah or are used only in passing; I relied on the Benjamite Gibeah.
Hosea's references (HOS 9:9, 10:9) allude to the old sin of Gibeah but state no event, so I left them out.
1SA 7:1 and 2SA 6:3-4 mention the house of Abinadab 'in the hill' or 'in Gibeah'; the ark's keeping there may belong to a different place, so I did not use it.
